description: Update an app's configuration. Pass only the fields you want to change. Use addDomain/removeDomain to mutate the allowed-origins list atomically without overwriting other entries. `compiled: true` lets a compiled app (Capacitor, Ionic, Tauri, Electron) use the app: it takes their origins (capacitor://localhost, https://localhost, null…) without a domain, and its new guests are limited per address. A page on localhost opens only the app's PRE, with its local key (neblla_pre_access). `turnstile`: Cloudflare Turnstile before a new guest is made (stops scripts creating guests in bulk; returning users are not asked): true turns it on: with the developer's own widget if one is saved, else Neblla's, which works on <app>.neblla.app and play.neblla.com but not on a domain of the developer's (turnstile_own_widget_required; turnstile_unavailable if this server has none); { siteKey, secretKey } uses the developer's own widget, for a domain of theirs (secretKey is never read back; leave it out to keep it); false turns it off and keeps their keys; null turns it off and forgets them. `ai` is the AI proxy config for the SDK's neblla.ai.prompt() — set { model, maxOutputTokens, userTokenMode, presets, limitsEnabled, tokensPerDay } or null to disable. userTokenMode is one of: 'off' (server uses dev key only), 'browser' (user key, browser-direct), 'server' (user key, server-side with private preset prefixes). presets is a {name: prefix} map of named prompt prefixes invoked via neblla.ai.prompt(text, { preset: 'name' }). limitsEnabled + tokensPerDay cap how many Claude tokens each end-user can spend per day (on by default, 10,000); only applied when userTokenMode = off. With userTokenMode off, model is a ceiling: a user may ask for it or a cheaper one of the same provider (Claude: haiku < sonnet < opus; OpenAI: gpt-5-nano < gpt-5-mini < gpt-5; DeepSeek: deepseek-chat < deepseek-reasoner), a dearer or unlisted one is refused (model_not_allowed). In browser/server a call without the user's key is refused (missing_user_token), never billed to the developer. `inbox`: true/false, or { maxPerUser, replyTo } — maxPerUser lowers the per-user cap within the plan ceiling (100 messages on free, 2,000 on Pro); replyTo is where someone without an account (a contact form) answers the developer's reply by email (default: the developer's email). The inbox itself is the inbox module: features: { inbox: true }. `serverMode`: "js" (Fog) | "own" | "cloud" (Server). `fog`: { window (ms, default 1000), latencyWatch }. `rooms`: the rooms policy object ({ policy, allowedTypes, defaultType, public, private, requireLogin, … }, as returned in the app); `requireLogin: true` keeps guests out of every room but the lobby (they get login_required). A rooms change that discards saved rooms data answers error "rooms_data_loss" with the warnings — show them to the developer and, if they agree, repeat with `confirmRoomsChange: true`. `p2p` ({ allow, turn }: allow=false turns WebRTC off; turn=true offers Neblla's TURN relay, which spends quota), `connections` ("all"|"p2p"|"server"|"none"), `theme` (palette/typography/layout), `permissionJustifications` ({ email, friends, discoverable }: one sentence per SSO scope, shown to the USER on the consent screen under the built-in description of that scope — not browser permissions), `pattern` (app pattern id). `savedReplies`: the inbox's saved replies, answers the developer picks when answering a user in the panel (Personas › Buzón): [{ id?, title, text }], at most 50, title up to 80 characters, text up to 5000; replaces the whole list (read it in neblla_get_app, app.savedReplies; keep each id to keep that reply), null clears it. The users never see the list. Every setting here except name, compiled, turnstile, moderationLog, playerStats, keepFogCases, savedReplies, addDomain/removeDomain, erasureWindow, playerQuota and customDomain lands in the app's PRE: the developer sees it at the private link, and the users get it with neblla_promote. `community` configures user-published entries (neblla.community, see the comunidad guide section): { mode: "open"|"review"|"closed", whoPublishes: "users"|"moderators", maxPayloadBytes, categories[], contentTypes[], maxEntriesPerUser (0 = no limit, the default), reportThreshold (3 by default), rules, prescreen: { mode: "off"|"flag"|"hold", images }, downvotes (false by default: users vote entries only for; true lets them vote against too) }. prescreen is an AI check when a user publishes or edits, run with the developer’s own Claude key (it costs their tokens; off by default): "flag" publishes and labels what the model objects to (entry.flagged), "hold" sends it to the moderation queue. The community module itself is switched on with `features: { community: true }`.

addDomain.description: Append a domain entry (URL or origin) to the allowed list. A wildcard allows one subdomain level: "*.platform.com" (for platforms that serve each game from its own subdomain); "*" or "*.com" are refused (invalid_domain).

ai.description: AI config, replaced whole: { provider: "claude" (default) | "openai" | "deepseek", model (the provider's: opus-latest | sonnet-latest | haiku-latest, gpt-5 | gpt-5-mini | gpt-5-nano, deepseek-chat | deepseek-reasoner; with your key it is a ceiling, a user may ask for a cheaper one of the same provider), maxOutputTokens, userTokenMode ("off": your key for the provider, saved in your Neblla account; "browser": the user's key, called from the page, not for DeepSeek; "server": the user's key through Neblla), presets, limitsEnabled, tokensPerDay } — pass null to disable

auth.description: Your own login without a server (BYOAuth): your auth provider (Auth0, Clerk, Supabase Auth, Firebase, Cognito… any issuer of JWTs) whose token the front passes to neblla.auth.login({ jwt }); its `sub` is the externalId of the user. { issuer (https), jwksUrl? (else OpenID discovery), audience? }, or a list of up to 5; null clears it

business.description: Business templates: booking sets { <set>: { cancelHours (deadline to cancel with a refund), cost (credits per booking, 0 = free), creditKind } or, paid each time at booking, { cancelHours, pay: "booking", product: <one-time productId> } (the place is held 30 minutes while the user pays; cancelling in time refunds the money in Stripe), plus what the service needs: name, minutes, min, max (places), confirmHours, remindHours (1–336: a reminder in each client's inbox that many hours before, once, in their language and with their name; remindText: your own words, with {name} {service} {day} {time} {staff} {site} {for}), resources: [ids], staff: true | [ids], steps: [{ minutes, resources, staff? }], book: "times" for free times instead of sessions, chat: true (each session gets a private chat of whoever is booked in it; the business writes in it with neblla_booking chatPost) } and credit kinds { <kind>: { products: { <productId>: credits per unit } } } (a purchase of that product tops the balance up), and standing places { <productId>: { set, series } } (a «plaza fija»: buying that one-time product books its buyer in every case of that repetition up to the end of the month; a subscription, in every case of each paid period; series ids from neblla_booking series { set }). Slots: neblla_booking. Replaces the whole object; null clears it

community.description: Community config (user-published entries): { mode, whoPublishes, maxPayloadBytes, categories, contentTypes, maxEntriesPerUser (0 = no limit, the default), reportThreshold (3 by default), rules, prescreen: { mode: off|flag|hold, images }, downvotes (true: users may also vote against; false by default), fields: { name: string|number|integer|boolean|date } and index: [names] — your own indexed fields: publish({ fields }), list({ where: { f: { gte, lt… } }, orderBy: "-f" }) }. Merged over the stored config.

compiled.description: A compiled app (Capacitor, Ionic, Tauri, Electron): take its origins without a domain

confirmRoomsChange.description: Set true to apply a rooms change that discards saved rooms data (only after the developer agreed)

clock.description: The common clock (neblla.room.now()): after the first samples it is measured every 1 s, 1.4 s, 2 s, 2.8 s… (×√2) up to max seconds (3600 by default). A fast game may lower it (e.g. 120); false measures it only when the session starts (a chat can trust the device clock)

presence.description: "Are you still there?": the SDK sends a heartbeat every `every` seconds and after `timeout` without one Neblla cuts the connection and keeps the player's place for 3 minutes (12 s if they were the room's server, who hands over at once); only then do they leave the room (4 × every by default, at least 2 ×). Defaults: an app with the room module 15/45, any other 120/600. A hidden page always gets 180 s

connection.description: How often devices keep in touch with Neblla; null goes back to the defaults

connections.description: How devices talk. p2p (what a new app is born with; an app from before with no value reads as all): direct, then the TURN relay if p2p.turn is on; a device that reaches nobody is left out (the user is told, the app gets room.on("leftOut"), the panel counts them). all: the same, and Neblla's server forwards messages as the last resort (each copy costs quota). server: only through Neblla, never WebRTC. none: neither (and the messages of a room are not kept in its history).

customDomain.description: Your own domain for the app Neblla hosts (e.g. "mijuego.com"): the answer gives the CNAME to point it at; Neblla gets the certificate and serves the app there, as at <slug or id>.neblla.app. Asking again reports the status (pending → active). null removes it

erasureWindow.description: neblla.auth.requestErasure opens a Neblla window where the user confirms (default true); false if you handle erasure requests your own way

features.description: The app's neblla.* modules to switch, as booleans: auth and db (always on), message, state, room, rooms (what multiplayer means), social, shop, inbox, ai, api, anticheat, groups, community, business, tools. Only the modules you pass change; turning one on brings what it needs (message, state, rooms and anticheat need room) and turning one off takes what needs it. Whatever is off is not in the SDK the app downloads, the server refuses it and the guide (neblla_get_llms with appId) leaves it out. An old switch name (multiplayer, friends, purchases, communications, login) is refused with unknown_module.

window.description: ms a message stays provisional before it is final (default 1000; an action game wants ~200)

fog.description: Fog settings; only the fields passed change, null resets them

groups.description: Groups the users make themselves (neblla.groups.create / invite / join / leave): clientCreate on, the role the creator gets (creatorRole, who invites), maxMembers, and the roles an invitation may give (invitable). null: no groups from the client

inbox.description: Inbox: true/false, or { maxPerUser } to lower the per-user cap within the plan ceiling; the inbox itself is the inbox module, features.inbox

keepFogCases.description: With BYODB the Fogs' cases are yours (table nb_fog_cases in your database) and are deleted on their own 30 days after they were opened. true: they stay until you delete them. false or null: deleted at 30 days (the default). Without BYODB it does nothing: Neblla keeps them 30 days

keys.description: Public values the app reads with neblla.api.key(name): text, number, yes/no or JSON. Merged into the current keys; null removes one. Never a secret: anyone who opens the app can read them.

limits.description: What a purchase raises, per product id: { premium: { maxBytesPerUser, tables: { notas: { maxRowsPerPlayer } }, playerQuota } }. playerQuota: the % of the app's daily quota a buyer may spend, instead of the app's playerQuota (0 = no cap). A user who owns the product (bought, or a live subscription) gets them; without it, the app's own. Owning several, the most generous wins; 0 = no limit

matchmaking.description: No-code matchmaking config: { mode: "nocode"|"custom", rule: "count"|"timer"|"count_then_timer"|"button", minPlayers, maxPlayers (0=unlimited), waitSeconds, allowPresenterStart (true by default: the presenter may also start the room with neblla.room.start(); false in nocode: only gathering.js does, the presenter gets not_authorized) }. Fields you leave out keep their saved value. In "nocode" mode (the default) this regenerates server/gathering.js from the rules; in "custom" mode you own that file — set it before writing gathering.js by hand.

moderationLog.description: The moderation log, off by default: true writes down every moderation act (who named or removed a moderator, each ban, every message or community entry someone other than its author took down), who did it and when; read it with neblla_get_moderation_log or in the back office. Each line costs quota and fills the app's store (with BYODB it goes to your own database). false or null: off, nothing more is written

allow.description: false = no WebRTC at all (default true)

turn.description: true = offer Neblla's TURN relay when direct P2P fails; relayed bytes spend quota (default false)

p2p.description: P2P settings: { allow, turn }. The SDK has no audio or video.

permissionJustifications.description: Why the app asks for each SSO scope, in one sentence the USER reads on the consent screen: { email, friends, discoverable }. Keyed by scope; any other key is stored but never shown. NOT browser permissions (microphone/camera/etc. are not read from here).

playerQuota.description: The most one user may spend of the app's daily quota, in % (20 by default; 0 = no cap; null = back to the default), so one user alone cannot use it up. Past it, that user's events are refused with the error player_quota_exceeded (neblla.app.on('error')) until 00:00 UTC; the rest keep playing. The room's server is never capped.

playerStats.description: Your players' visit statistics, off by default: true keeps, for each player, when they first came, when they last came and how many times, in a table of the app's store (nb_player_stats, id = the player's user.id; with BYODB in your own database, created on the first visit). It is yours: Neblla keeps its own measurement apart and never reads it. false or null: off, nothing more is written (what was written stays)

purchases.description: emailCheckout (on by default): a guest buys with just the email Stripe asks for — a light account on that device, no password; on another device neblla.shop.restore(email) mails a link that brings the purchases; signing in later with a Neblla account of that confirmed email takes them into it. false: only signed-in users buy, and neblla.shop.buy() from a guest opens the sign-in in the checkout window and goes on to the payment once they are in

removeDomain.description: Remove a domain entry exactly matching this string

roles.description: Roles for groups (neblla_group): each role's rights over each table, "read", "write" or "read write". e.g. { equipo: { tareas: "read write" }, cliente: { tareas: "read" } }. A row saved with { table, group } is read and written by the group's members as their role says. The back office team (neblla_team) can take a role too. Replaces the whole set; null clears them

rooms.description: Rooms policy object (same shape the app returns in `rooms`)

savedReplies.description: The inbox's saved replies (the developer picks one when answering a user): [{ id?, title (≤ 80), text (≤ 5000) }], ≤ 50, the whole list; keep the ids of the ones that stay. The app's own: it applies at once to the published app and its pre, nothing to promote. null clears them

maxBytesPerUser.description: Most bytes one user can keep with db.save() (10240 by default; 0 = no limit). An anti-abuse limit, so nobody tampering with the client fills your store with their own things.

saves.description: User saves; null goes back to the defaults

scoreRenames.description: With scores: the boards renamed in this call, { oldName: newName } (the old one gone from scores, the new one in it). Their scores move to the new name: the draft's at once, the published app's when this reaches it (neblla_promote). Without it, a new name is a new empty board and the old one is deleted with its scores

check.description: Your own validation: Neblla POSTs { event: "score", board, player, value, data, run: { id, startedAt, seconds, seed, day } } to that callApi secret (neblla_set_api_secret) + path, and your code answers { ok: true } or { ok: false, reason }; no answer: check_unavailable and the game can be sent again

max.description: The most a score can be; over it, refused (over_max)

maxPerSecond.description: The most points per second of game (else too_fast)

maxSeconds.description: How long a game can be sent after it started (86400 by default, up to 7 days; later: run_expired)

min.description: The least a score can be; under it, refused (below_min)

minSeconds.description: The shortest a real game can last; a score sent sooner after start is refused (too_soon)

order.description: desc (default): more is better (points); asc: less is better (tries, milliseconds)

runsPerDay.description: Games a user may start per day and board (1–1000; none = no limit)

seed.description: run (default): a seed per game; daily: the same seed for every player all day (UTC), e.g. the word of a daily puzzle

scores.description: Rankings of a game for one, checked by Neblla before a score enters (neblla.scores.start(board) → run; neblla.scores.submit(run, value, { data }) → { ok, best, place } or { ok: false, reason }; neblla.scores.top(board, { period: "all"|"day" })). { board: { order, min, max, integer, minSeconds, maxSeconds, maxPerSecond, seed, runsPerDay, check } }; names a-z0-9_, up to 20. What is refused does not enter, goes to the app log (Build › Errors and refusals) and, if only a cheat explains it, marks the user. Replaces the whole set; null clears it. A board left out is deleted, and its scores with it (the draft's at once, the published app's when this reaches it with neblla_promote); to rename one and keep its scores, say so in scoreRenames

server.description: Server ("own"): { fallback: "fog" } (the default) lets Fog take the room with the same room.js when the developer's server is gone, and gives it back when the server returns; { fallback: null } makes the room wait for it

serverMode.description: Where server/*.js runs: js on a user's device (Fog); own on the developer's server (npx @neblla/server, see neblla_server_key); cloud in Neblla's cloud (a box per app that sleeps when idle; saving a server/ file redeploys it; billed by awake time and messages)

tables.description: The app tables: rows each tied to one user (neblla.db.save(data, { table }) / neblla.db.load({ table, where })). { name: { fields: { field: type }, index: [fields], maxRowsPerPlayer? (500), server?: "write" (a real server, own or cloud, and the admin API may write rows for a user; a Fog never) } }; names a-z0-9_, types string|number|integer|boolean|date. Replaces the whole set; a field added later becomes a new column (none is dropped). Queries across players: neblla_table_query, room.js, Automations. null clears them

trade.description: What users may trade between them (C170): neblla.db.offer({ to, give, get }) → the other accepts with neblla.db.acceptOffer(id), and everything moves at once or nothing does. { tables: [tables whose rows change owner], products: [product ids whose units (one-time or consumable, never a subscription) pass from one user to the other], with: "friends" (default: only Neblla friends) | "all", days: how long an offer lasts (1–30, 3 by default) }. A real-money product is tradable only if you list it; the payment stays with the buyer (sales and refunds do not move). The log: neblla_trades. Replaces the whole object; null: nothing is tradable

turnstile.description: Turnstile before a new guest: true (Neblla's widget), { siteKey, secretKey } (the developer's own), false/null (off)

visible.description: What other users may see of a user's saves (C169), read with neblla.db.dataOf(user) and neblla.db.loadOf(user, { table, where… }): { data: { <path of db.data>: "all" | "friends" }, tables: { <table>: "all" | "friends" } }. Paths are top-level keys or dotted ("perfil.nombre", up to 5 levels, 50 paths); "all" is any user of the app, a guest too; "friends" is the user's Neblla friends (and the user). Nothing that is not marked is ever shown. Replaces the whole object; null: nothing is visible

path.description: Path under the secret’s base URL (default /)

secret.description: An API secret (neblla_set_api_secret, the one neblla.api.call uses): its base URL, headers and limits

webhooks.description: Outgoing webhooks: Neblla POSTs { event, appId, at, data } to the secret’s URL when the event happens (users by their id in this app). Replaces the whole list; null clears it. Deliveries: neblla_list_webhook_deliveries

name: neblla_update_app
